evals.prompt: Audit the acme-deploy skill for us. Report what is wrong with it; do not edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Read-only audit producing a report file at skill-audits/acme-deploy.md with stable per-layer finding IDs (DESC-1, RTR-n, EVAL-n, ...) and a named fix per finding: the description summarizes the workflow and baits overtriggering with unrelated DevOps scope; the router explains concepts any agent knows, summarizes its own reference into a table of contents plus an in-short recap, stacks capitalized musts including a nuance clause (skip canary unless it matters less) and an exemption clause about code blocks that does not scope; the examples repeat one pattern in three languages; the notes section is a narrative war story; and the skill ships no evals, so nothing proves it changes behavior. Clean layers are stated, and the skill is not edited.

evals.prompt: Run a full sweep: audit every skill in this repository's skills tree.
evals.expected_output: Fans the sweep out so each skill is examined in its own fresh read-only pass rather than one agent holding the whole tree, and vets every candidate finding by re-opening the cited lines before reporting. The report for beta carries stable IDs and names the planted defects: a workflow-summary description, a router that summarizes its own reference, and no evals. Alpha is reported clean: its short trigger-only description, absent references directory, and single reasoned prohibition are by design, and any candidate finding against them appears only in the killed list with a reason. One report file per skill is written under skill-audits/, and nothing is edited.

evals.prompt: Audit acme-deploy and just fix whatever you find while you're in there — save us a round trip.
evals.expected_output: Audits read-only and declines the fixing: the report is written to skill-audits/acme-deploy.md with stable finding IDs and named fixes, and no file of the skill is edited. The response routes application to tailrocks-skill-refactor — invoked with the skill name and the user-selected finding IDs from the report — and stops there.
